Hi Emily / team - looping in a short technical readout based on the traffic profile and the targets. High-level recommendations to hit 99th <= 250ms for streaming while keeping unit cost reasonable: 

1) Continuous batching
- Use Redwood's continuous batching layer tuned to your request size distribution. For 1-2KB prompts, a batching window of 8-12ms with adaptive batch size (up to ~64 tokens aggregated) keeps tail latency low while increasing GPU utilization.

2) Prefix / KV caching
- Enable per-session KV caching for repeated context (user system prompts, recent turns). We expect ~15-25% token savings on your chat flows given the session reuse in the profile.

3) Quantization profiles
- Recommend a mixed profile: int8 quant for non-critical model variants and int16 (or bf16) for flagship variant. For some candidate workloads we see negligible quality delta for int8 with significant cost reduction (~2.5x cheaper token cost).

4) Model variants and routing
- Primary variant: large-quantized (gpt-large-q8) for standard responses.
- Fallback/high-quality: gpt-large (bf16) for elevated quality paths (e.g., long-form summarization).
- Use smart routing: latency-sensitive short-turns -> quantized model pinned to low-latency nodes; long-form/rare heavy work -> high-cost high-quality nodes.

5) Concurrency and autoscaling knobs
- Start with target per-GPU concurrency 48 streams, scale horizontally on queue latency > 20ms. For your 500 qps global peak, estimate ~8-12 GPUs in Dedicated mode depending on quantization and batching efficiency.

6) Streaming optimizations
- Token-level streaming with early flush for first tokens (send header/first token as soon as generated) reduces perceived latency. Avoid large final-token-only aggregation.

Cost sketch (very rough)
- With int8 quant + continuous batching + caching, projected token-unit cost reduction ~55-65% vs baseline bf16 non-batched serving.

Next steps
- Marissa: we can share a short simulation and a 1-page cost estimate by EOD today (attaching).
- Emily/Carlos: confirm if region split (US/EU) is required for initial rollout - that will change the sizing.

Attachment: cost-estimate-v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
